messages.author: 0ebb124842957335
messages.subject: undocumented Subread behavior
parts:
I notice that Subread 1.4.6-p1 has been released and it has this release note:

Distance between two neighboring genomic variants is allowed to be as small as 1bp (it was 16bp).

Looking at the documentation of the previous version of Subread, I see that this aspect of the aligner's algorithmic flow has not been noted in the past. I, for one, have been assuming that the aligner did not have such a requirement and have used the Subread for alignment purposes where neighboring genomic variants (mismatches) are possible (e.g., in data of cancer tissues).

It seems, then, that the aligner may have certain odd behaviors that are not documented and may be unknown to a user, and one therefore has to be careful about using Subread for identifying sequence variations (mutations in cancer, RNA editing, etc.).

Please correct me if I am wrong, and thanks again for the software which does work very well and fast for many other purposes.

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: undocumented Subread behavior
parts:
Subread aligner uses a lot of parameters to control its sensitivity and specificity in mapping reads and detecting genomic variants. We only made some of these parameters be tunable by users to ease the use of our program and our documentation is provided for these parameters only.

We have released version 1.4.6-p2 on Mar 24 and a new parameter called "--minDistanceBetweenVariants" was added to allow users to specify the minimum required distance between neighbouring variants. We found that allowing a very small distance may greatly increase the running time of the alignment and therefore we decided to allow users to tune this parameter to suit different needs.

We apologize if this parameter has caused any problems to your projects. Every aligner uses a lot of parameters and usually only part of the parameters are documented. I hope you find that our documentation for Subread aligner is better than many other software programs, but it is certainly our intention to make it more complete and accurate.

Thank you for using Subread and we look forward to having more comments/suggestions from you.

Wei

parts: Thanks for clarifying upon this, and for adding the new parameter to Subread.
